diane_customer: Hey team — our on‑prem Dedicated instance (vpc/private) is dropping streaming SSE responses mid‑payload and then client reconnects get 401s. Happens behind customer corporate proxy. Partial tokens delivered, then the connection just closes.

tara_support: Hi Diane, sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the client-side logs and the initial curl you used to reproduce? Also which model + server version?

Diane_customer: Repro steps: 1) Start stream with curl from inside corp network:
```bash
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \\n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\n  -d '{"model": "open-compat-1", "input":"long prompt...", "stream":true}' \\n  https://private.example.corp/api/v1/generate/stream
```
2) After ~20–40s SSE stops sending new data, client sees EOF. Sometimes reconnects work, sometimes immediate 401. Server logs show the session still active for a few seconds then closed.

mike_infra: Is the corp proxy doing TLS inspect or altering TCP MSS? Common pattern: MTU/MSS path leads to fragment loss with middleboxes. Any tcpdump or proxy logs? Also which kernel version / NIC offloads on the ingress box?

Diane_customer: Proxy does TLS inspect and uses a BlueCorp proxy appliance. I pulled a short tcpdump at the ingress: saw reassembled packets, occasional duplicate ACKs, and a stray RST from proxy IP when payload size grows. I can share PCAP.

alex_ml: Could be chunk boundary/flush semantics + the proxy buffering. When SSE messages are small we’re fine; large payloads or steady token flow cause streaming to be treated as long-lived connection and some proxies drop after buffer thresholds. Two immediate checks: 1) try lowering keepalive idle/interval on client and server 2) set SSE to send periodic heartbeat comments (":\n") every 10s to keep proxy alive.

tara_support: Also: the 401 on reconnect suggests session token rotation or short-lived auth cookie on our side. Diane, are you using any session resumption token or a short TTL token for streams? If yes, we should confirm token rotation policy on private control plane.

Diane_customer: We use a rotating session token tied to the stream ID with 30s window. We thought that would improve security. Maybe that's why reconnections get 401. Can we disable rotation?

mike_infra: For immediate mitigation: ask customer to extend token TTL (e.g., +5m) and enable heartbeat comments. For root cause, collect: ingress tcpdump, nginx/haproxy proxy logs (buffer states), and SST metrics from private control plane (connection drops, auth rejects). Also check MSS/MTU on path: try setting MTU 1400 on the ingress NIC to see if fragmentation disappears.

alex_ml: One more angle — some corp proxies convert SSE to buffered long polling if they detect content‑length issues. Look for proxy header rewriting (Transfer-Encoding or Content-Length). If they buffer, once buffer limit hits they may close connection. If you can share the proxy config or logs showing "buffered" or "timeout", that helps.

diane_customer: Uploaded PCAP and proxy logs to the support share (link omitted). Changed token TTL to 10m and added heartbeat comments — still saw one mid‑stream drop but client resumed with new token ok. There's a proxy log entry right before the drop: "upstream buffer exceeded, closing connection".

tara_support: Thanks, that log is telling. Next steps: our ops team will try two server-side patches in a canary: 1) emit 10s heartbeats by default for private deployments behind proxies; 2) keep a short grace window for token rotation on stream reconnects (90s).

ingress-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started to 3 nodes in region-eu-private at 2024-07-26T15:12Z.

mike_infra: Also advise customer to increase proxy buffer or treat the SSE endpoint as streaming (disable full buffering). If they can't change proxy, MTU tweak + heartbeat should be a reliable workaround.

diane_customer: Appreciate it. Will coordinate with proxy team to raise buffer and test MTU. I'll post results in this thread. :pray:
